papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md (Surrogates are modest): 'Matsuda versus clamp r 0.73', OGTT-derived indices listed but not weighed.
papers.full_text_shows: r = 0.73 is for the composite index against whole-body glucose disposal in the clamp, in 153 mixed subjects (62 NGT, 31 IGT, 60 T2DM). The index was developed and tested in the same sample, with no independent validation set. The fasting-based ISI(HOMA) had r = 0.69 in the same data, so the post-load index is only a little higher; the mean glucose / mean insulin ratio had r = 0.02. Two-column PDF extraction garbled the correlation tables, but the abstract and text numbers are readable.
papers.quote: provides a reasonable approximation of whole-body insulin sensitivity from the OGTT
papers.key_numbers: n=153 (66 men, 87 women, age 18-71, BMI 20-65); composite index vs clamp r=0.73 (P<0.0001); ISI(HOMA) r=0.69; Cederholm r=0.62; Belfiore r=0.54; G/I ratio r=0.02 (NS).
papers.role_in_work: Example of a post-load (OGTT-derived) index validated against the euglycemic clamp; the Matsuda index derivation paper.
papers.design: Cross-sectional method-comparison; 75-g OGTT and euglycemic clamp with [3-3H]glucose in random order; correlation analysis.
papers.population_and_size: 153 adults in San Antonio, with NGT, IGT or type 2 diabetes; ethnic mix not stated in the parts read.
papers.measure_type: Post-load: insulin and glucose during 75-g OGTT (0, 30, 60, 90, 120 min) combined into an index; compared with the fasting-based HOMA index.
papers.assay_or_platform: Plasma insulin by radioimmunoassay; clamp with tracer glucose.
papers.quality_note: Derivation and test in one sample (optimistic r); pooled over glucose-tolerance groups, so r partly reflects the wide range; not a test of any clinical decision.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md (Surrogates are modest): 'TG/HDL-C fails in African Americans'.
papers.full_text_shows: Supported for TG and TG/HDL-C as markers of insulin resistance in 98 African American adults with BMI 25 or more (aged 20-50). The reference was the minimal-model insulin sensitivity index from a frequently sampled IV glucose tolerance test, not the clamp, and insulin resistance was defined as the lowest tertile of that index in this sample. Fasting insulin did well (AUC 0.85) in the same data, so the paper also supports fasting insulin as the better marker here (in-sample tertile).
papers.quote: In African Americans, TG levels and TG-HDL-C ratio are not reliable markers of insulin resistance.
papers.key_numbers: n=98; AUC fasting insulin 0.85 +/- 0.04, BMI 0.72, waist 0.71, TG 0.55, TG/HDL-C 0.56; lipid criteria met by 17, only 7 in the insulin-resistant tertile (sensitivity 17%).
papers.role_in_work: Evidence that the non-insulin surrogate TG/HDL-C does not track insulin resistance in one population.
papers.design: Cross-sectional diagnostic-accuracy analysis (ROC) against FSIVGTT minimal-model insulin sensitivity.
papers.population_and_size: 98 African American men and women, aged 20-50, BMI 25 or more, no diabetes (from 125 recruited).
papers.measure_type: Non-insulin surrogate (fasting TG, TG/HDL-C); the comparator fasting insulin is fasting-based; reference test is a stimulated (IV glucose) minimal-model index.
papers.assay_or_platform: FSIVGTT with MINMOD; insulin by assay not read in detail.
papers.quality_note: Single population, small sample, tertile-defined resistance (relative, not a clinical threshold), age 20-50 only; no financial disclosure.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md (incremental prediction): 'the Gutt index in Framingham ... biostatistician reports no gain, but ... not verified whether insulin was included' and 'AROC unchanged when HOMA-IR or insulin added'.
papers.full_text_shows: The open question is settled: insulin was included. The complex models added fasting insulin with 2-h OGTT glucose and CRP, or the Gutt index (OGTT glucose and insulin plus weight), or HOMA-IR and HOMA beta-cell. AROC stayed at 0.850-0.854 versus 0.85 for the simple clinical model. The outcome is incident type 2 diabetes (7-year, 160 cases), not cardiovascular disease, and the model was not a CVD prediction model.
papers.quote: Complex clinical models showed no further improvement in model discriminations (AROC, 0.850-0.854)
papers.key_numbers: 3140 participants, 160 incident T2DM; personal model AROC 0.72; simple clinical 0.85 (0.881 with continuous covariates); complex models 0.850-0.854; 10 jackknife iterations AROC 0.73-0.91.
papers.role_in_work: Null for incremental value of insulin-based measures (fasting insulin, Gutt, HOMA-IR) over simple clinical variables for predicting diabetes.
papers.design: Prospective community cohort (Framingham Offspring), prediction model development with AROC comparison; no external validation.
papers.population_and_size: 3140 middle-aged, 99% white men and women with OGTT at baseline, no diabetes; 160 new T2DM cases over 7 years.
papers.measure_type: Mixed: fasting insulin, HOMA-IR and HOMA beta-cell (fasting-based) and the Gutt index (post-load: OGTT glucose and insulin).
papers.assay_or_platform: Fasting and 2-h OGTT insulin; assay not read in detail.
papers.quality_note: Outcome is diabetes, not CVD; white population; AROC differences between nested models tested with a small number of cases; funded by NIH.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md (incremental prediction): 'Health ABC ... an OGTT measure (not specified in the files), fasting insulin and HOMA-IR added to fasting glucose did not improve prediction, so it is also a fasting null'; listed as a post-load prediction result.
papers.full_text_shows: The OGTT measure is the 2-hour plasma glucose, not insulin. Insulin was measured only fasting. So there is no post-load insulin result in this paper: it is a fasting insulin / HOMA null plus a 2-h glucose null. Fasting insulin and HOMA measures were not associated with incident heart failure in the adjusted analyses; fasting glucose was the strongest predictor.
papers.quote: none of the other markers -- fasting insulin, 2 hour post challenge glucose levels. Hemoglobin A1c, and HOMA-based IR and β cell function assessment -- provided additional prognostic information.
papers.key_numbers: n=2386 without diabetes, age 70-79; additional markers did not improve a base model with fasting glucose (all Wald P>0.4); fasting glucose adjusted HR 1.10 per 10 mg/dL (1.02-1.18).
papers.role_in_work: Null for incremental value of fasting insulin/HOMA (and 2-h glucose) beyond fasting glucose for incident heart failure.
papers.design: Prospective cohort (Health ABC), Cox models and c statistics, incremental models with Wald test.
papers.population_and_size: 2386 community-dwelling adults aged 70-79 without known diabetes (white and Black), Pittsburgh and Memphis.
papers.measure_type: Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR/HOMA-beta (fasting-based). The OGTT contribution is 2-h glucose only, no post-load insulin.
papers.assay_or_platform: Insulin by Abbott IMx microparticle enzyme immunoassay; glucose by YSI 2300; HbA1c by Bio-Rad Variant.
papers.quality_note: HF defined by hospitalisation (undercount); elderly only, authors say not transferable to the general population; incremental test was P-value based, not delta C.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md and claims EV-27 / EV-07: 'HOMA-IR and fasting insulin lost association after HDL-C adjustment ... read as redundant given HDL-C'.
papers.full_text_shows: Matches the abstract. Extra detail: insulin, HOMA-IR and TG/HDL-C remained associated after adjusting for all traditional risk factors except HDL-C, and added weak discrimination in simpler models; none added discrimination to a model of age, race and HDL-C (delta c-index 0.001-0.002). NRI in the full model was small and non-significant (HOMA-IR 0.002, CI -0.015 to 0.019).
papers.quote: Measures of insulin resistance were no longer associated with CVD risk after adjustment for high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol
papers.key_numbers: 15,288 women, 894 CVD events (5.8%) in 10 years; HR per doubling after age/race: insulin 1.21, HOMA-IR 1.19, TG/HDL-C 1.35; after HDL-C adjustment insulin 1.06 (0.98-1.16), HOMA-IR 1.06 (0.98-1.15), TG/HDL-C 1.11 (0.99-1.25); insulin and HOMA-IR correlated r=0.99.
papers.role_in_work: Incremental-value null for fasting insulin and HOMA-IR (and TG/HDL-C) for CVD in women.
papers.design: Prospective cohort from WHI Biomarkers studies; Cox models, c-index, NRI, IDI.
papers.population_and_size: 15,288 postmenopausal women without CVD, AF or diabetes; 1993-1998 baseline.
papers.measure_type: Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR (fasting-based); TG/HDL-C (non-insulin surrogate).
papers.assay_or_platform: Fasting serum insulin from stored samples; assay not read in detail.
papers.quality_note: Women only, hormone-trial subcohorts, one baseline measurement; insulin and HOMA-IR are nearly the same variable here (r=0.99).

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md and claim EV-28: 'Wang 2022 (per-SD HR about 1.04 in normal glucose tolerance with a CI including 1). Skeptic files disagree on some Wang figures'; listed under incremental prediction.
papers.full_text_shows: The figure is correct: HR per 1 SD 1.04 (0.92-1.18) in NGT, 1.12 (1.06-1.18) in prediabetes, 1.15 (1.09-1.21) in diabetes, P interaction 0.011. This is an association study with interaction by glucose tolerance, not an incremental-value or discrimination study. Main models were adjusted for age, sex, education, alcohol, smoking, physical activity and diet quality, not for BMI, lipids or blood pressure. Follow-up was short (mean 3.6 years).
papers.quote: each 1 SD of HOMA-IR associated with no significant excess CVD risk in participants with normal glucose tolerance
papers.key_numbers: 111,576 adults, 2,708 CVD events; all participants HR 1.15 per SD (1.11-1.19), Q4 vs Q1 1.36 (1.22-1.50); NGT n=28,890 Q4 vs Q1 1.03 (0.82-1.30); prediabetes Q4 vs Q1 1.23 (1.07-1.42); diabetes Q4 vs Q1 1.61 (1.30-2.00).
papers.role_in_work: Shows HOMA-IR association with CVD depends on glucose tolerance status; cited as a null in NGT.
papers.design: Nationwide prospective cohort (China Cardiometabolic Disease and Cancer Cohort); Cox models by glucose tolerance stratum.
papers.population_and_size: 111,576 Chinese adults aged 40 and over without glucose-lowering drugs; baseline 2011-2012.
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (HOMA-IR from fasting insulin and glucose); glucose tolerance status from fasting and 2-h OGTT glucose and HbA1c (no post-load insulin).
papers.assay_or_platform: Fasting insulin assay not read in detail; glucose oxidase or hexokinase; 75-g OGTT for glucose.
papers.quality_note: Short follow-up; NGT stratum has fewer events and wide CI (a null in NGT is partly a power issue); association, not prediction; self-reported/ adjudicated mixed outcome including heart failure.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md and claim EV-29: 'HOMA-IR is linked to incident T2D (HR 1.87), non-fatal MACE (HR 1.46) and hypertension (HR 1.35) in a 38-cohort meta-analysis, with no association with fatal MACE.'
papers.full_text_shows: Numbers are correct. Heterogeneity is very high for T2DM (I2 94%) and non-fatal MACE (I2 84%), and cut-offs differ between studies (quartile comparisons or established cut-offs). Fatal MACE had HR 1.31 (0.96-1.77), a wide interval with a similar point estimate, so 'no association' means 'not shown', not 'absent'. The authors themselves call the clinical utility questionable because predictive values are not standardised.
papers.quote: questionable degree of clinical utility due to the lack of standardization of predictive values
papers.key_numbers: 38 studies, 215,878 participants; T2DM HR 1.87 (1.40-2.49) I2 94%; non-fatal MACE HR 1.46 (1.08-1.97) I2 84%; hypertension HR 1.35 (1.15-1.59) I2 16%; fatal MACE HR 1.31 (0.96-1.77) I2 50%; cancer mortality HR 1.00 (0.91-1.11) from 3 studies.
papers.role_in_work: Support for a real but modest association of HOMA-IR with outcomes.
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohorts (PROSPERO CRD42020187645); Newcastle-Ottawa quality; 94.7% rated good quality.
papers.population_and_size: 38 cohorts, 215,878 adults, healthy or with metabolic syndrome components.
papers.quality_note: Association only (adjustment sets vary), high heterogeneity, no test of incremental value; no conflict of interest declared.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md and claim GL-34: consensus 'giving TyG moderate evidence for CVD prediction'.
papers.full_text_shows: The statement is in the precision-prognosis section of a systematic review of longitudinal studies of people with type 2 diabetes. It concerns CVD prediction in people who already have T2D, which the project text does not say. The consensus rates TyG high predictive utility with moderate evidence; it does not recommend TyG as a clinical test. The consensus also supports C-peptide (detectable, antibody-negative) in selecting under-30 non-obese people for monogenic diabetes testing (random or unspecified-timing C-peptide), which is relevant to existing C-peptide rows rather than to this claim.
papers.quote: we found high predictive utility for N-terminal pro b-type natriuretic peptide (high evidence), troponin T and triglyceride-glucose (moderate evidence)
papers.key_numbers: 416 studies in the CVD-prognosis review; 195 novel nongenetic CVD biomarkers, 12 improved c-statistic/NRI/IDI in more than one study.
papers.role_in_work: Consensus-level statement on TyG as a prognostic biomarker (non-insulin surrogate) in T2D.
papers.design: International consensus report built on systematic reviews (ADA/EASD Precision Medicine in Diabetes Initiative).
papers.population_and_size: For the TyG statement, people with T2D in 416 longitudinal studies; mostly European ancestry.
papers.measure_type: Non-insulin surrogate (TyG, fasting); C-peptide mentioned for monogenic diabetes testing (timing not specified in the passage read).
papers.quality_note: Consensus report, not a guideline; the evidence base is observational; TyG statement is population-specific (T2D).

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion.md and claims EV-18 / EV-25: 'TyG added to Framingham gave a pooled C-index gain of 0.0004 (-0.0092 to 0.0100), very low GRADE, 0.0051 (0.0007-0.0094) without one dominant cohort'; 'Pooled Liu 2026 was against Framingham'.
papers.full_text_shows: Numbers match. But the pooled analysis combined five cohorts with different base models: SCORE2-Asia, pooled cohort equations and three Framingham-type models, so it is not 'against Framingham'. Heterogeneity was I2 99.1%. The excluded study (Barzegar) is the one with a negative calculated change (-0.018); the other four calculated changes are +0.003 to +0.011. The authors call the effect clinically trivial and rate certainty very low. In the authors' own cohort, TyG quartiles gave IDI 0.0034 (P=0.023) and a significant event NRI, while continuous TyG gave none; some p-values and CIs in the text look inconsistent (for example event NRI 0.0476, CI -0.0048 to 0.0913, P<0.05).
papers.quote: the overall certainty of evidence for the incremental C-index change in the main analysis was rated as very low
papers.key_numbers: Own cohort n=4,665 (210 CVD events, median 6 years): C-index 0.731 to 0.732 (continuous TyG), 0.739 (quartiles, P=0.21); pooled 5 studies 27,329 participants, 2,457 events, delta C 0.0004 (-0.0092 to 0.0100), I2 99.1%; without Barzegar 0.0051 (0.0007-0.0094).
papers.role_in_work: Incremental-value result for TyG (non-insulin surrogate) over risk scores; a null or trivial gain.
papers.design: Cohort study (CHNS 2009-2015) plus systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42024525061).
papers.population_and_size: CHNS adults aged 45-80 without CVD, n=4,665; meta-analysis of 5 cohorts from China, US, Spain and Iran.
papers.assay_or_platform: Fasting triglyceride and glucose in CHNS 2009 laboratory data.
papers.quality_note: Outcome self-reported or proxy-reported MI or stroke in CHNS; attrition 9.6-29% in cohorts; change in C-index for Barzegar was calculated from two models, not reported; very low certainty (GRADE).

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, 'Incremental prediction is thin...' bullet (post-load results in the files; Health ABC); claims.csv EV-14
claim_issues.issue: Health ABC is described as a post-load prediction result with an unspecified OGTT measure. The full text shows the OGTT measure is 2-hour glucose; insulin was fasting only. It is not a post-load insulin result.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Health ABC (PMID 19700136; full text read; heart-failure outcome in 2386 adults aged 70-79 without diabetes): fasting insulin, HOMA-IR and 2-hour OGTT glucose, each added to fasting glucose, did not improve prediction. This is a fasting insulin/HOMA null; no post-load insulin was measured.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, same bullet; claims.csv EV-15 and EV-28 (Framingham Offspring, PMID 17533210)
claim_issues.issue: It says it was not verified whether insulin was included, and lists it with CVD prediction results. Full text: insulin was included (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, Gutt index), and the outcome is incident type 2 diabetes, not CVD.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Framingham Offspring (PMID 17533210; full text read): for 7-year incident type 2 diabetes (160 cases in 3140 mostly white adults), complex models with fasting insulin, the Gutt index (OGTT glucose and insulin) or HOMA-IR had AROC 0.850-0.854, no better than the simple clinical model (0.85). Outcome is diabetes, not cardiovascular disease.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, Wang 2022 line under incremental prediction; claims.csv EV-28
claim_issues.issue: Wang 2022 is an association study with an interaction by glucose tolerance, not an incremental prediction study. The 1.04 figure is confirmed, but with follow-up of 3.6 years, a model without BMI, lipids or blood pressure, and a wide CI in the smaller NGT stratum.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Wang 2022 (PMID 35700159; full text read; association, not prediction): HOMA-IR per SD HR 1.04 (0.92-1.18) in normal glucose tolerance (n=28,890), 1.12 (1.06-1.18) in prediabetes and 1.15 (1.09-1.21) in diabetes (P interaction 0.011); mean follow-up 3.6 years; models adjusted for age, sex, education, alcohol, smoking, physical activity and diet quality.

claim_issues.issue: TyG 'moderate evidence' for CVD prediction applies to people with type 2 diabetes in that consensus, not to the general population. The consensus does not recommend TyG for clinical use. GL-34 also says 'Liu 2026 and ATTICA nulls', but ATTICA was a gain.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: ADA/EASD 2023 precision-medicine consensus (PMID 37794253; full text read): in its systematic review of CVD prognosis in people with type 2 diabetes, TyG was rated high predictive utility with moderate evidence. This is a statement about people with diabetes and about prediction, not reclassification; it is not a recommendation to use TyG clinically. Read next to the Liu 2026 near-null and the ATTICA gain.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, Liu 2026 bullet; claims.csv EV-18 and EV-25 ('Pooled Liu 2026 was against Framingham')
claim_issues.issue: The pooled estimate combines five cohorts with different base models (SCORE2-Asia, pooled cohort equations, three Framingham-type models); only the authors' own cohort and two others used Framingham-type models. Heterogeneity I2 99.1% is not stated. The excluded study is Barzegar, which has the only negative change.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Liu 2026 (PMID 42569452; full text read): in a meta-analysis of five cohorts (27,329 participants) using different base risk models (SCORE2-Asia, pooled cohort equations, Framingham-type), adding TyG changed the C-index by 0.0004 (-0.0092 to 0.0100), I2 99.1%, certainty very low; without the Barzegar cohort 0.0051 (0.0007-0.0094), which the authors call clinically trivial. In the authors' own CHNS cohort (n=4,665) continuous TyG added nothing (C-index 0.731 to 0.732); TyG quartiles gave IDI 0.0034 and an event NRI with P<0.05.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, 'Association is real but modest' (PMID 36181637); claims.csv EV-29
claim_issues.issue: Needs the heterogeneity and the wording on fatal MACE. 'No association' with fatal MACE has HR 1.31 (0.96-1.77), a wide interval, so it is 'not shown', not 'absent'. I2 is 94% for T2DM and 84% for non-fatal MACE.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: HOMA-IR (fasting-based) was linked to incident T2D (HR 1.87, 1.40-2.49, I2 94%), non-fatal MACE (HR 1.46, 1.08-1.97, I2 84%) and hypertension (HR 1.35, 1.15-1.59, I2 16%) in a 38-study meta-analysis (PMID 36181637; full text read); for fatal MACE the HR was 1.31 (0.96-1.77), not significant. Cut-offs differed between studies, and the authors describe clinical utility as questionable because predictive values are not standardised.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, 'Surrogates are modest' (Matsuda r 0.73, PMID 10480510); claims.csv MEAS-04
claim_issues.issue: r 0.73 is from the derivation sample itself (153 mixed subjects), against clamp whole-body glucose disposal, with no independent validation; the fasting-based ISI(HOMA) had r 0.69 in the same data.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: OGTT-derived indices are in the files but not weighed here (for example the Matsuda composite index against the clamp, r 0.73 in the 153-subject derivation sample, with no independent validation; the fasting-based ISI(HOMA) gave r 0.69 in the same sample; PMID 10480510, full text read).

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, 'Surrogates are modest' (TG/HDL-C fails in African Americans, PMID 15983289); claims.csv MEAS-02
claim_issues.issue: Needs scope: one small sample (n=98, BMI 25 or more, age 20-50), reference is FSIVGTT minimal-model index with resistance defined by tertile, and in the same data fasting insulin performed well (AUC 0.85).
claim_issues.proposed_wording: TG and TG/HDL-C did not identify insulin resistance in 98 African American adults with BMI 25 or more (AUC 0.55 and 0.56; FSIVGTT minimal-model reference, lowest tertile as resistant); fasting insulin had AUC 0.85 in the same sample (PMID 15983289, full text read).

notes: All nine local text files were read through grep and targeted passages, not every line. C001 text is a two-column extraction with garbled correlation tables; I relied on the abstract block and running text for numbers, and did not check Table 2-4 values beyond ISI(composite) 0.732 and the NGT subgroup lines. Quotes were copied from the extracted text (line breaks and hyphenation removed). C007, C010 and C034 are PDF extractions with some symbol loss (plus/minus signs); no number was judged wrong because of that. Assay details were not read for C007, C010, C034 and C088. No score proposals: none of these papers changes the evidence behind a U*/V* row. Not checked: the contents of usecases-verified.md row 45 beyond a grep hit (it concerns other papers). Tool calls used: 18 before writing, plus 2 writes.
